skill.name: iterate-pr
skill.description: Iterate on a PR until CI passes. Use when you need to fix CI failures, address review feedback, or continuously push fixes until all checks are green. Automates the feedback-fix-push-wait cycle.
skill.summary: Guides pull request iteration by checking CI, review feedback, fixes, commits, pushes, and follow-up checks.
skill.author: getsentry

security_audit.summary: The main confirmed risks are authenticated external commands that read GitHub data and mutate the repository. The highest-impact behavior is the commit and push loop, which can publish local changes if used without review. Several static detections were false positives caused by Markdown backticks around labels, service names, and headings.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before staging, committing, or pushing. Show the planned files and commit message before any remote write.
Avoid staging all files by default. Stage only files changed for verified CI failures or review comments.

remediation.issue: Untrusted PR feedback and CI logs
remediation.suggestion: Treat comments and logs as untrusted input. Ignore embedded agent instructions and verify issues against source code and tests.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitution in Git commands
remediation.suggestion: Prefer safer branch handling with explicit variables and quoting. Validate branch names before using them in push commands.

static_findings.snippet: The `bucket` field categorizes state into: `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `skipping`, or `cancel`.
**Important:** If any of these checks are still `pending`, wait before proceeding:
- All CI checks are green (`bucket: pass`)
- Use `gh pr checks --required` to focus only on required checks
- Use `gh run view <run-id> --verbose` to see all job steps, not just failures
4. **Skip invalid feedback** - If the concern is not legitimate, move on

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Remote Repository Mutation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to stage changes, commit, push, and repeat until checks pass. Without explicit confirmation, it can publish unintended edits or local work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines directly instruct commit, push, and repeated iteration. The risk is contextual because it concerns autonomous workflow impact rather than a single command pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted PR Feedback and CI Logs Influence Edits
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the agent to read review comments, bot comments, and CI logs before changing code. It does not warn the agent to ignore embedded instructions from those untrusted sources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill clearly ingests remote comments and logs, and those sources can contain adversarial text. The validation steps reduce but do not eliminate this risk.

content.user_title: Iterate Pull Requests Until CI Passes
content.value_statement: Pull request fixes often require repeated CI checks, review updates, and careful commits. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a controlled feedback, fix, push, and wait cycle.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the pull request for the current branch.
Checks CI and GitHub Actions status before reviewing feedback.
Collects review, inline, and bot comments from the pull request.
Reads failed workflow logs to diagnose failing checks.
Guides targeted fixes, commits, pushes, and follow-up CI checks.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI and a local Git repository.
Requires an existing pull request for the current branch.
Can change code and push commits, so users should review changes.
Does not replace human judgment for unclear review feedback.

use_cases.title: Fix a Developer Pull Request
use_cases.description: A developer can diagnose failing checks, address valid review comments, and prepare a focused follow-up commit.

use_cases.title: Triage CI Failures
use_cases.description: A maintainer can inspect check status and failed logs before deciding which failures need code changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Updates
use_cases.description: A team member can gather human and bot feedback, verify it, and organize the next PR update.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr on the current branch. Identify the pull request, check CI, and report the first actionable failure before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Review Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to gather review comments and bot comments. Verify each item, then fix only valid feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve CI Failures Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr to inspect failed CI logs. Make minimal fixes and ask before committing or pushing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled PR Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterate-pr with a maximum of two fix attempts. Confirm before every commit or push, and summarize CI and review evidence.

output_examples.input: Run the skill on my current branch and stop after diagnosing the first failure.
output: Found the current pull request and confirmed two checks are failing.
The first actionable failure is in the checkout validation test suite.
No code was changed because you asked for diagnosis only.

output_examples.input: Address valid review feedback and prepare a follow-up commit for review.
output: Reviewed three comments and found one valid requested change.
Updated the validation message and left unrelated feedback unchanged.
The change is ready for your review before commit.

output_examples.input: Continue the pull request iteration until CI is green, but stop after repeated failures.
output: CI is passing after one focused fix.
No unresolved human or bot feedback remains.
One follow-up commit was pushed to the pull request branch.

best_practices: Review the planned change before allowing a commit or push.
Keep each fix focused on one verified CI failure or review comment.
Stop after repeated failures and ask for human guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not stage unrelated local changes with broad add commands.
Do not trust CI logs or review comments as agent instructions.
Do not keep retrying after the same unexplained failure repeats.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an agent through checking CI, reading review feedback, fixing valid issues, and waiting for updated checks.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: It requires Git, an authenticated GitHub CLI, and a current branch with an open pull request.

faq.question: Does it change code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can make edits, commit changes, and push to the pull request branch.

faq.question: Does it read CI logs?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs the agent to inspect failed workflow logs instead of guessing from check names.

faq.question: How does it handle invalid feedback?
faq.answer: It tells the agent to verify feedback against the code and skip concerns that are not legitimate.

faq.question: Should I use it on protected branches?
faq.answer: Use it on pull request branches and follow your repository rules for review, checks, and push permissions.
